title: Backlog phase
description: Validates one backlog phase on its own, as a YAML mapping extracted from the backlog file (no front matter or section conversion applies). A phase is one session of work: what it changes (scope), how completion is observed (acceptance, verification), and what it locks while claimed (systems, deliverables, depends_on). The required fields are the portable core. The optional fields are the ones d-system uses, listed so their shape is checked when present. Other fields are allowed, so an adopting repository can add its own without editing this schema. The core is deliberately looser than d-system's own item definition (schemas/backlog.schema.json in d-system), which requires every core field plus sources, owner, priority, session_budget and next_action (not ideas), fixes identifier patterns and requires at least two acceptance conditions. Every phase in d-system's backlog validates here; check_schemas.py checks that. Whether an active phase must name an agent is left to the host repository's concurrency rule (d-system requires one only when more than one phase may be active at once).

id.description: Stable phase identifier, never renumbered. It names the branch and worktree of the session that claims it.

title.description: One concrete outcome achievable in one session.

plan.description: Identifier of the plan document this phase belongs to.

status.description: Execution state. Readiness is not a status: a queued phase is ready when every depends_on phase is complete.

systems.description: System identifiers this phase changes. Two active phases sharing a system may not run at once.

depends_on.description: Phase identifiers that must be complete before this phase starts. Empty when there are none.

scope.description: Bounded steps the phase carries out.

acceptance.description: Observable conditions that must hold for the phase to be complete. At least one here; d-system's own backlog schema requires at least two.

verification.description: Commands or concrete checks that show whether the acceptance conditions hold.

deliverables.description: Repository paths the phase plans to create or change. Two active phases sharing a path may not run at once.

sources.description: Other documents the phase draws on, such as the requirement it satisfies.

owner.description: Who answers for the phase. Not the agent that claims it.

session_budget.description: Sessions the phase is expected to take. d-system fixes this at 1.

next_action.description: The first useful step for whoever picks the phase up next.

agent.description: Identity of the agent holding the claim. Not allowed on a queued, deferred or cancelled phase. Whether an active phase must carry one is the host repository's concurrency rule, not this schema's.

blocked_reason.description: Why a blocked, deferred or cancelled phase is not running.

resume_when.description: The condition that releases a blocked or deferred phase.

session.description: Identifier of the session record that completed the phase.

completion_evidence.description: Paths that exist and prove completion. Kept separate from deliverables, which are planned paths.

result.description: The verification outcome actually observed, written at completion.

ideas.description: Identifiers of captured ideas this phase acts on (d-system-specific).
